impact:
deliberatePlan/deliberateCode fall through to plain failover whenever session_id is present, but the MCP server instructions tell callers to always pass session_id from review_plan into review_code. So in deliberate/deliberate-deep mode only the first review of a lifecycle deliberates; plan→code and every re-review after fixes runs single-provider with no indication (deliberation block simply absent). Fix options: attach a deliberation skipped marker (e.g. { skipped: 'resumed_session' }), or deliberate anyway (resume primary's thread, fresh secondary review). Natural to bundle with the open per-call deliberation toggle / mode-surfacing item from the v1.4.0 handover.

LIVE-CONFIRMED 2026-07-01 (probe loop, real Gemini via CLI against dist 1.4.0): fresh review created session 045f02a1…; `review-code --session <id>` with mode=deliberate returned a successful result with NO deliberation block and no marker — silently single-provider. Repro: .reviewbridge.json {provider: gemini, mode: deliberate}, run review-code fresh, then again with --session. Bug category: silent no-op (of the deliberation layer) / swallowed signal.
resolution: Fixed in T-028. Two-pronged: (1) deliberate-on-resume — a resumed review in deliberate mode now resumes the owning leaf (T-027 routing) while the other leaf reviews fresh, then combines, so plan→code lifecycles keep deliberating instead of silently going single-provider; the combined result keeps the resumed owner's session id. (2) review_mode is stamped on every result (single/failover/deliberate/deliberate-deep), so the absence of a deliberation block is never ambiguous. Plus a per-call `deliberate` toggle (MCP + CLI). Regression tests in deliberation.test.ts + composite.test.ts.
title: Deliberation silently disabled on resumed sessions — recommended session_id workflow defeats the feature
